docs.text: ADR-0022 — Syntactic monoid representation and canonical normalization ¶ Status: Accepted Date: 2026-09-24 Context ¶ Professor requirement #62 asks for the syntactic monoid constructed from word-induced transformations. The supplied mature extension names DFA-only SyntacticMonoidMixin.syntactic_monoid() and reports three elements for its executed modulo-three DFA. It specifies neither the public transformation representation nor the return container. The broader analysis mentions SyntacticMonoid and TransitionMonoid as concepts, without a class API. Closing transformations over an arbitrary DFA's stored states instead yields that representation's transition monoid . Inaccessible or equivalent states can enlarge it, while partial transitions do not define total maps. The syntactic monoid of a language is isomorphic to the transition monoid of its minimal complete DFA. Verified requirement #60 already builds that DFA from the distinct left quotients, including an empty quotient when needed. Decision ¶ Expose ExtendedDFA.syntactic_monoid() -> frozenset[tuple[int, ...]] through SyntacticMonoidMixin only. First call residual_automaton() ; do not redo minimization or close over the source transition table. The residual states must be exactly q0, ..., q(n-1) ; their numeric indices define each tuple's positions and destinations: entry i == j means qi -> qj . This tuple and frozenset representation is an Automatix public API decision , not a type specified by the supplied mature material. The set has no iteration order. Include tuple(range(n)) as the empty word's identity, including for an empty alphabet. Construct one total generator for each input letter from the complete residual DFA. A queue closes the discovered transformations by appending each letter. If tau_w is the current tuple and tau_a the letter tuple, the appended word wa has tau_(wa) = tau_a ∘ tau_w , encoded by next[i] = tau_a[tau_w[i]] . Extending each discovered element by each letter generates every word by induction from the empty word; all-pairs composition is unnecessary. The method is a pure query. It does not mutate the source or #60's fresh residual automaton and does not cache its result. Its output is a language invariant up to monoid isomorphism; literal tuple equality across arbitrary renamings is not promised. Partial source DFAs are normalized through #60's empty residual. Source-inaccessible and equivalent states disappear. Alternatives considered ¶ Direct closure on self would calculate a potentially larger source transition monoid and mishandle partial transitions. complete().minimize() can also give a suitable minimal complete DFA but duplicates normalization policy already verified by #59/#60 and provides less direct q-index semantics. A mutable set or mapping would weaken the immutable mathematical API. Dedicated public monoid or transformation classes, multiplication tables, and general algebraic operations are unsupported by the supplied contract. automata-lib 9.2.0 has no syntactic-monoid closure operation to delegate to. Consequences ¶ If the canonical DFA has n states, the alphabet has s letters, and the monoid has m transformations, closure uses expected O(m*s*n) time and O(m*n + s*n) space, in addition to #60's construction cost and storage. The explicit result can be large: m <= n**n . The mature three-state DFA produces exactly identity and two rotations, matching its observed size 3. Related requirements ¶ Implements final professor requirement #62 using verified #59/#60. Does not change their public behavior or introduce a standalone algebra framework. Supersedes ¶ None.

docs.text: ADR-0023 — Read-only distinguishability round table ¶ Status: Accepted Date: 2026-09-27 Context ¶ Primary #29 requires iterative marking of distinguishable DFA state pairs. The mature documentation adds a complete pair table with marking rounds, but does not specify the public return type of pair_table() . Existing distinguishable_states() returns a set of frozenset pairs and does not retain rounds. Primary #29 and #30 must preserve their verified semantics. Decision ¶ Use one private reverse-dependency breadth-first table-filling engine for both the original query and the new API. A final/nonfinal pair enters at round 0. If a symbol leads from a pair to a round-r pair, that pair can enter at round r+1. Breadth-first processing records its first, shortest distinguishing-word length. A missing mark denotes equivalent states. pair_table() -> Mapping[frozenset[FAStateT], int | None] returns every unordered pair of original states, including equivalent and inaccessible ones. Keys are inserted in a deterministic state-label order and the mapping is protected by MappingProxyType. For a partial DFA, the completion sink participates in the private analysis but never becomes a public pair key. distinguishable_states() keeps its existing set return type and is exactly the subset with non-None rounds. pair_table_str(show_round=True) -> str renders a triangular ASCII table with no terminal newline. Its header has one leading space for one-character state labels, matching the exact string explicitly requested for M3. The mature PDF prints three leading spaces in that same line; the prompt's later, explicit expected output controls this presentation-only discrepancy. With show_round=False , marked pairs display X ; unmarked pairs display . in both modes. print_pair_table(show_round=True) -> None prints that same string and a newline. A one-state DFA has no table cells and renders as the empty string. Arbitrary heterogeneous state labels use the same deterministic ordering key as the public mapping. Alternatives considered ¶ Return a mutable dict: callers could change an analysis result and mistake it for automaton state. Return only marked pairs: loses equivalent-pair information needed for a complete triangular view. Run separate analyses: duplicates #29's algorithm and can disagree on partial DFA semantics. Reproduce the PDF's three-space header: differs from the task's explicit one-space expected string; the mathematics and cells agree. Consequences ¶ The shared analysis uses O(|Q|² * |Sigma| + V + |Q| log |Q|) expected time and O(|Q|² * |Sigma| + M) space, where V/M account for completion and validation. Round numbers are deterministic, independent of hash-set iteration order. Formatting adds O(R) time and memory for R rendered characters; printing adds O(R) output work. Related requirements ¶ M2–M4 and primary #29–#30. Supersedes ¶ None.

docs.text: ADR-0024 — Bounded order search for regex conversions ¶ Status: Accepted Date: 2026-09-27 Context ¶ The mature documentation exposes DFA-only to_regex_optimum() and to_regex_arden_optimum() , but specifies neither a complete elimination order search nor a tie-break rule. Both executed three-state outputs are observable contracts. Requirements #53 and #54 already have verified converters whose exact, more verbose results must remain unchanged. Decision ¶ Extract each existing conversion engine into a private order-parameterized method. The original public methods call those engines with their established lexical order. The two optimum methods try the first 24 permutations of states sorted by the established heterogeneous-safe key. For Arden, only accessible states participate, as in #54. Every raw candidate is parsed and rendered through the private #49 immutable Regex AST, which removes redundant grouping and applies its existing identity rules. Represent epsilon alone as the established empty string. Rank candidates by length, then lexicographically. The three-state mature fixture tries every order. The results are exactly (b|ab*ab*a)* and (ab*ab*a|b)* . The limit of 24 keeps larger DFA instances usable; neither result is promised globally minimal. Alternatives considered ¶ An unbounded search over all permutations has factorial work for every DFA and quickly becomes impractical. A new state-elimination or Arden solver would duplicate verified #53/#54 logic and risk changing their public outputs. A fixture-specific rewrite would not define a general algorithm. Consequences ¶ For n states, k = min(n!, 24) orders are tried. The state-elimination path makes O(k n³) label updates plus k GNFA constructions; the Arden path makes O(k m³) coefficient updates for m accessible states. Intermediate strings and AST comparisons can grow exponentially. The chosen result is stable for ordinary and heterogeneous states. No automaton is mutated or cached. Related requirements ¶ M5 and M6, reusing primary #49, #53 and #54. Supersedes ¶ None.

docs.text: ADR-0025 — Cached-method temporary lifetime patch ¶ Status: Accepted Date: 2026-09-27 Context ¶ automata-lib 9.2.0 depends on cached_method >=0.1.0. The installed cached_method 0.1.0 descriptor stores an lru_cache callable per instance; that cache holds only a weak method. When a cached method is called on a temporary automaton, its returned callable can outlive the object before invocation. The executed native DFA expression (d - d).isempty() raises RuntimeError: Bound object has been garbage collected . The mature documentation explicitly fixes this through an import-time runtime patch. Decision ¶ During import of automata_extensions , install one idempotent replacement for cached_method.__get__ . The replacement delegates all cache lookup and creation to the original 0.1.0 descriptor, then returns a short-lived callable holding the instance strongly. Class-level descriptor access is unchanged. Neither the instance nor its cache stores this new wrapper; the underlying cache retains its weak reference and its cache_info/cache_clear operations. Reject an unknown version or a conflicting descriptor patch instead of changing uninspected behavior. Alternatives considered ¶ Change automata-lib or site-packages source: forbidden by project rules. Patch each affected upstream method: duplicates work and misses future cached methods. Bind every temporary in caller code: cannot satisfy the mature public chained-call contract. Consequences ¶ All automata-lib cached_method descriptors in the process benefit after one Automatix import, including native DFA. This is a deliberately global, version-targeted runtime compatibility patch; no algorithm-result cache is added. Tests verify idempotence, cache hits, temporary calls and garbage collection. Related requirements ¶ M9; the fixed upstream dependency is recorded in ADR-0001. Supersedes ¶ None.

docs.text: ADR-0026 — Standalone Graphviz subprocess renderer ¶ Status: Accepted Date: 2026-09-27 Context ¶ The mature documentation proposes render_diagram(agraph, filename, prog="dot", fmt=None) for an upstream pygraphviz AGraph returned by show_diagram() . It avoids drawing through pygraphviz's C binding when native DLLs conflict. Existing Automatix dot()/svg()/pdf()/png() serve a different in-memory export path and remain unchanged. The mature helper does not have a fixed package module. Decision ¶ Expose render_diagram from automata_extensions.utils , implemented in utils/render.py beside utils/patches.py . Accept AGraph structurally through its string() -> str operation. Infer the format from the output suffix when omitted, defaulting to PNG. Search for the selected Graphviz program under the current Python environment's Library/bin on Windows or bin on POSIX, then fall back to PATH. Pass DOT as subprocess text input, capture errors, raise FileNotFoundError for a missing executable and RuntimeError for a failed render, and return the requested Path. Never invoke a shell or draw through the pygraphviz binding. Alternatives considered ¶ Add a method to every automaton: the mature text proposes a standalone helper, not a mixin API. Put the function in VisualisationMixin: it operates on an AGraph rather than an automaton and would mix two rendering paths. Require a fixed Conda location: unnecessarily ties the API to one machine and prevents use with a system Graphviz installation. Consequences ¶ The helper writes exactly the requested output artifact; tests use temporary directories. A fake subprocess verifies arguments and errors, and a real integration check renders PNG, SVG and PDF. The existing in-memory rendering pipeline remains intact. Related requirements ¶ M10 and primary visualisation requirements #40–#41. Supersedes ¶ None.

docs.text: ADR-0027 — Stable video layout and independent render cadence ¶ Status: Accepted Date: 2026-09-27 Context ¶ M11 initially rendered a new Graphviz PNG for every input symbol. That recomputed layout, produced one still per logical step and used the public fps argument as the MP4 frame rate. The video had no in-between motion, and its changing Graphviz label consumed space needed by the automaton. The M11 redesign must preserve execution semantics, animate() HTML and the existing meaning of fps while producing a stable, readable 16:9 video. Decision ¶ Keep fps as logical input steps per second and add a keyword-only render_fps: int = 30 for MP4 frames per second. Build the trace through the verified execution_trace() and accepts() operations. Ask Graphviz once for its plain output from the existing DOT source. Its node centers, edge labels and cubic spline control points become an immutable layout. Sample each spline by traveled distance, including self-loops, to move a small marker. Expand each logical step into movement and arrival moments, with a short initial pause and final result hold. Use Pillow to compose a fixed 1280×720 scene from that layout and timeline. Draw the graph, initial pointer, final double circles, curved arrows and labels as a stable base; add state emphasis, moving marker, word cells and acceptance badge on each frame. Render at twice the target resolution and downsample once per frame. Pillow is a declared Python dependency. FFmpeg remains an optional external runtime executable and still encodes the MP4 inside a temporary directory before replacing the requested destination. Alternatives considered ¶ Re-run Graphviz for every frame: allows style changes in DOT but moves nodes and curves and scales poorly with 30-fps timelines. Parse SVG paths and rasterize SVG per frame: requires another SVG renderer or a more complex path/transform parser. Graphviz plain already exposes cubic control points and labels in a small documented text format. Launch a browser to record the HTML animation: less deterministic and conflicts with the browser-free M11 contract. Change fps to mean video frame rate: silently breaks the existing M11 public API. Consequences ¶ The graph layout is computed once and remains fixed; motion follows the actual Graphviz spline. Very high logical step rates can leave too few render frames for visible intermediate motion, but still preserve input semantics. Fixed output resolution is isolated in the private renderer for a future 1920×1080 option. Existing SVG/PNG/PDF exports and HTML animation do not change. Tests cover normal and loop splines, partial DFA blocking, empty words, accepted/rejected results, video metadata and no mutation. Related requirements ¶ M11 visual redesign, primary #16 and #40–#41, ADR-0014. Supersedes ¶ None.

docs.text: ADR-0028 - Accepting runs of epsilon-free NFAs ¶ Status: Accepted Date: 2026-10-16 Context ¶ INF302 Enonce_TD.v04 exercise 38 asks to list accepting executions and compute N(A,u), their count for one input word. The user selected this feature after a coverage audit and explicitly accepted starting without epsilon transitions. It is supplemental TD work, not a change to the professor requirements numbered #1-#62 or previously verified features. automata-lib 9.2.0 has no colliding accepting_runs/count_accepting_runs API. NFA.read_input_stepwise merges active states; _get_input_path selects one path. DFA.count_words_of_length counts words, not executions. None can implement this contract by delegation. The mature reference contains no documented accepting-run API to reproduce. Decision ¶ Expose AcceptingRunsMixin on ExtendedNFA only, before the upstream NFA: accepting_runs(word: str) -> Iterator[tuple[FAStateT, ...]] count_accepting_runs(word: str) -> int A run contains the initial state and one state per consumed character, ending in an original final state. Destination sets contain no parallel copies of an identical edge; runs are distinguished by their state history. An empty word has exactly one accepting run if the initial state is final. Unknown characters and dead ends yield no runs/count zero. Validate the string and absence of real epsilon edges eagerly, even for unreachable edges and empty words. Raise TypeError for a non-string and ValueError for an epsilon edge. An empty epsilon destination set is not an edge. Do not automatically eliminate epsilon transitions: language equivalence does not preserve the number of execution paths. Use iterative DFS for lazy enumeration, with an iterator stack and a single mutable local prefix; yield immutable tuple snapshots. Never merge histories or sort heterogeneous state names. Destination iteration order is deliberately not a stable-order API. Every call has independent state. Count using the natural-number recurrence c_0(initial)=1 and c_(i+1)(r)=sum(c_i(q) for each q --word[i]--> r). Keep only the current and next dictionaries. Sum over final states after consuming the word. Python integers preserve exact large multiplicities. Neither query mutates the automaton, populates a persistent cache, determinizes or calls the other query. Alternatives considered ¶ Count by enumerating runs: exponential even when dynamic programming needs only a small active-state set. Use active-state sets: loses multiplicity when branches merge. Memoize a recursive counter: introduces recursion limits and unnecessary state/history storage; a two-layer recurrence is simpler. Support epsilon paths now: cycles can produce infinitely many runs and require another mathematical contract, outside the agreed first scope. Put the feature in ExtendedFA: deterministic targets and regex-labelled GNFA edges require different semantics; this API is specifically NFA. Consequences ¶ Enumeration can be exponential because its output is exponential. It validates in O(|Q|+n), then takes O(P+A (n+1)) time for explored prefix extensions P and A accepted runs. DFS auxiliary references are O(n+1); retaining the output requires O(A (n+1)) additional references. Counting takes O(|Q|+n+sum_i E_i) with unit-cost arithmetic, for matching edges E_i from each active layer. It retains O(|Q|) integer entries. Arbitrary-precision additions cost O(B) for B-bit counts; integer storage can take O(|Q|*B) bits besides state references. All lookup bounds assume expected constant-time hashing. No algorithm-result cache is introduced. Tests check the exercise-38 occurrence identity and product-square law, independent exhaustive state-sequence enumeration, merged branches, empty words/languages, dead ends, heterogeneous/None states, epsilon rejection, immutability, iteration independence and long words. Upstream NetworkX rejects None as a node during NFA simulation; the independent language check for that fixture uses the existing determinization, without changing upstream or the recognition API. Related requirements ¶ Supplemental TD38; existing #16 execution trace and #43 NFA intersection. See usage and mathematical contract . Supersedes ¶ None.

docs.text: ADR-0029 - Complete DFA construction from normalized regex derivatives ¶ Status: Accepted Date: 2026-10-16 Context ¶ After TD38 the user asked to continue the confirmed missing functionality. TD51.1-3 require both Thompson and a derivative construction. Regex already has one-symbol derivatives, but no full derivative automaton. Upstream automata-lib 9.2.0 offers regex -> NFA -> DFA rather than this construction; no public name collision was found. The mature reference documents no direct derivative builder. Existing ADR-0015 keeps its syntax and API. Raw structural derivative equality is insufficient for repeated exploration: unions can reassociate, reorder and repeat terms. Regex. str is also not a lossless serialization: an internal empty language and the literal empty-set glyph can both display as the same string. Decision ¶ Expose Regex.to_dfa() -> ExtendedDFA without new parameters. Its alphabet is the frozen alphabet already validated by Regex. Keep this conversion at the regex layer rather than a mixin over unrelated automaton classes. A private normalization module recursively flattens unions, deduplicates their terms structurally and orders them by their unambiguous dataclass representation. Concatenations flatten without reordering; existing AST smart constructors handle epsilon/empty identities and trivial stars. Apply normalization to the initial AST and to every computed derivative. No semantic language-equivalence oracle or global cache is introduced. Existing Regex.derivative and display outputs are not changed. Run BFS over normalized ASTs. Each concrete state is an immutable Regex value with the original alphabet. For every state and alphabet character, call its derivative method and intern the normalized resulting AST within this call. Mark a state final using the existing AST nullable predicate. The returned ExtendedDFA is complete and has only reachable states. Include the empty-language sink exactly when reachable. Minimality is not promised; the existing minimize() remains available. The finite-similarity argument is the classical derivative construction: associative, commutative and idempotent union canonicalization suffices for finite exploration for classical regular expressions; the additional identities preserve language. See Owens, Reppy and Turon (2009), section 4.1, https://doi.org/10.1017/S0956796808007090. This is a termination argument, not a polynomial-state or minimality guarantee. Alternatives considered ¶ Convert through Thompson or subset construction: produces a DFA but does not supply the independently requested derivative algorithm. Compare raw ASTs: misses union similarity and risks unbounded syntax growth despite finitely many language quotients. Compare rendered strings: conflates empty-language nodes and literals. Replace every existing smart constructor: changes existing observable derivative and conversion outputs beyond the authorized feature. Public nullable/simplify APIs or semantic minimization during discovery: unnecessary contracts and algorithms for the selected construction. Consequences ¶ For R reachable states and s symbols the graph has R s edges. Track all AST transformation, ordering, hashing/equality and nullability costs C explicitly; time is O(s log s + R s + C + V), including constructor V. Space is O(R*(s+1)+S+W+V_space), with retained AST size S and temporary workspace W. State counts and expression sizes can be exponential; the existing recursive AST operations retain Python's depth limits. Tests cover all TD51 expressions, equivalence with independent automata-lib and existing Thompson construction, every transition's quotient rule, nullable final states, reachable completeness, empty alphabets/languages, Unicode, ambiguous/reordered unions, sink identity, immutable fresh results, unchanged derivative renderings and composition with existing transformations. Mocks ensure no Thompson or subset algorithm is used by the builder. Related requirements ¶ Supplemental TD51, existing #49 derivatives and #51 Thompson construction. See usage . Supersedes ¶ None. Complements ADR-0015 without changing its accepted contracts.

docs.text: ADR-0030 — Présentation vidéo « Fil de lecture » ¶ Status: Accepted Date: 2026-11-16 Contexte ¶ L'utilisateur a validé le croquis « Fil de lecture » puis demandé des mouvements moins mécaniques et un suffixe souligné rouge, à pleine opacité, lors d'un refus. Le titre, le panneau encadré, la légende du mot et les badges remplis n'apportaient pas d'information utile. Décision ¶ Conserver le placement Graphviz unique, la composition Pillow suréchantillonnée, FFmpeg et les cadences publiques d'ADR-0027. Changer uniquement la présentation. Le mot occupe l'angle supérieur gauche. Les caractères consommés sont composés à 25 % d'opacité sur le fond ; le suffixe refusé reste à 100 % avec traits rouges. Le verdict visible est toujours « Refusé » pour les deux formes de rejet. Une phase continue par étape pilote une interpolation quintique de la distance sur la spline, une pulsation du caractère, le fondu source/destination et le halo d'arrivée. Une boucle conserve son état actif pendant le mouvement. Le compteur privé step compte désormais les caractères effectivement consommés : une transition absente n'incrémente jamais ce nombre. Un refus après lecture complète utilise le dernier caractère comme repère visuel du verdict ; il ne transforme pas cette transition valide en transition absente. Pour ε, seul le verdict porte la couleur du résultat. Conséquences ¶ Aucun nouvel argument public, changement du langage reconnu, mutation de l'objet ou dépendance. Les exports graphiques et le lecteur HTML restent inchangés. Les mots longs ont une fenêtre de 18 caractères ; l'affichage n'implique pas consommation des caractères masqués. Les polices de quelques tailles sont des ressources locales à un export, pas des caches d'algorithmes sur les automates. Supersedes ¶ ADR-0027 seulement pour le marqueur mobile, les cartes de caractères et le badge rempli. Son architecture et ses garanties d'encodage restent en vigueur.

docs.text: ADR-0031 — Découverte locale des outils vidéo ¶ Status: Accepted Date: 2026-11-16 Contexte ¶ Un noyau de notebook peut utiliser le bon Python Conda sans avoir le dossier Library/bin dans son PATH. L'export trouvait déjà FFmpeg mais Graphviz échouait, obligeant l'utilisateur à ajouter un chemin personnel dans chaque notebook. Décision ¶ Partager la découverte privée de dot et ffmpeg : PATH en priorité, puis répertoires conventionnels relatifs à sys.executable . Aucun chemin utilisateur codé en dur, aucune mutation de os.environ ou de la configuration globale de graphviz. Invoquer directement l'exécutable Graphviz trouvé avec -Tplain , entrée/sortie UTF-8, arguments séparés et sans shell. Le DOT reste celui du moteur commun ; placement, composition et encodage atomique ne changent pas. L'argument filename devient facultatif, avec animation.mp4 comme défaut relatif au dossier courant. Un dossier existant désigne animation.mp4 dans ce dossier. Les chemins explicites vers un MP4 gardent leur comportement et leur type de retour Path. Aucun dossier manquant n'est créé implicitement. Alternatives et conséquences ¶ Modifier globalement PATH ou DOT_BINARY interférerait avec le notebook et les autres exports. Installer automatiquement des outils est hors périmètre. Les outils absents restent des erreurs explicites. Les tests exécutent de vrais exports avec PATH vide, contrôlent les trois formes de destination et vérifient que l'environnement du processus est inchangé. Supersedes ¶ Complète ADR-0027 et ADR-0030 pour la découverte des exécutables et la destination facultative ; les décisions visuelles restent inchangées.

docs.text: Vidéo « Fil de lecture » — design validé ¶ Le croquis interactif et ses corrections ont été approuvés dans la conversation le 16 novembre 2026, avec demande explicite d'implémentation. Intention ¶ Une vidéo sobre où seuls le mot, le graphe et le verdict portent l'information. Mot en haut à gauche, sans titre ni légende. Symboles lus à 25 % d'opacité ; symbole courant légèrement pulsé, fond discret et trait inférieur. Graphe fixe, tracé progressif des transitions avec accélération/décélération, fondu entre états et halo léger à l'arrivée. Aucun gros marqueur mobile. Le verdict final est « Accepté » ou « Refusé », accompagné d'une coche/croix. Transition absente : arrêt au dernier état réel, soulignement rouge et opacité 100 % du symbole bloquant et de tout le suffixe non lu. Aucun état puits ajouté. Refus en état non final après lecture complète : dernier symbole souligné rouge à 100 %, repère du verdict, sans prétendre que sa transition était invalide. Mot vide : ε puis verdict ; pas de faux symbole refusé. Approches ¶ Trois croquis : Ligne claire (traits simples), Focus (état plein et point mobile), Fil de lecture (soulignements et fond discret). L'utilisateur a choisi Fil de lecture puis demandé un mouvement moins mécanique et le marquage rouge du suffixe refusé. Le libellé « Bloqué » a été explicitement remplacé par « Refusé ». Architecture et limites ¶ Conserver Graphviz pour l'unique placement, Pillow pour les images et FFmpeg pour MP4. Modifier uniquement la présentation vidéo privée et sa timeline. API export_animation_video(word, filename, *, fps=1.0, render_fps=30) inchangée, ainsi que animate() HTML. Aucun changement de langage reconnu ni mutation. 1280×720, traits et labels de l'automate conservés, rendu suréchantillonné 2×. Fenêtre glissante pour mots longs, sans réduire les caractères à l'illisible. Choix d'implémentation : fond ivoire, accent vert canard, rouge doux et cadence publique existante. Les ellipses indiquent les caractères hors champ. Vérification ¶ Tester prefixe consommé/suffixe refusé, refus final, mot vide, mouvement intermédiaire, boucle, transition absente, mots longs et cadre stable. Suite pytest complète, mypy strict, vrais MP4 acceptation/refus/blocage et inspection de leurs images. Dépendances et encodage atomique inchangés.
docs.title: Vidéo « Fil de lecture » — design validé
